result.title: Practical Non-Stationary Graph Gaussian Processes
result.summary: Gaussian processes on graphs provide a principled framework for prediction and uncertainty estimation, but modelling heterogeneous networks often requires balancing flexibility against parameter complexity. Variability at a node may reflect useful signal that should propagate through the network, unreliable measurements whose influence should be suppressed, or a mixture of both. We introduce Variance-Coupled Gaussian Processes (VCGPs), which use a positive auxiliary signal to modulate graph interactions through a single learned coupling exponent. The exponent controls how strongly high-variability nodes propagate or attenuate information, while a cluster-wise extension accommodates different regimes within the same graph. Under stated structural assumptions, we characterize the unique stationary-rescaling point of the basic family, where correlations match those of a stationary graph kernel while node-dependent variances remain. Experiments on traffic, air-quality and weather datasets show competitive prediction and uncertainty estimation relative to stationary and per-node non-stationary baselines, with the largest gains on networks requiring multiple coupling regimes. Stationary correlations after variance rescaling remain sufficient on some data, and performance depends on the auxiliary signal and model selection.

AI.brief_summary: 提出方差耦合高斯过程（VCGP），用单一可学习耦合指数借助正辅助信号调节高方差节点在图上传播或衰减信息，并给出按簇分段的扩展以适配同一图内的多种耦合机制。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「按节点不确定性决定信息传播强度」的建模思路，可能为 LVR 中不可靠视觉证据的抑制与筛选、以及可靠性加权如何影响 latent 状态更新提供远域启发，可供核查能否迁移到区域或 token 级的证据门控。
